addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - API usage, tool use, Anthropic SDK usage. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- qemu-runner: Use this agent when you need to run a RISC-V ELF binary through Andes QEMU and get its output. Always use this agent instead of running QEMU directly, as it handles the semihosting fd 9 output capture quirk in Claude Code's sandbox.

Examples:

- assistant: *builds a test binary*
  assistant: "Let me use the qemu-runner agent to execute the binary and check the output"

- user: "Run this ELF at VLEN=512"
  assistant: "I'll use the qemu-runner agent to run it" (Tools: Bash, Read) (Tools: Bash)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

attachment.content:
- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.
- libnn-optimizer: Autonomous optimization workflow for libnn RISC-V neural network library functions
in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",
"libnn", "FPGA perf", "optimization loop", "validate config",
"phase gather/baseline/iterate/evaluate", "perf test", or references opt/config.toml,
opt/state.json, or any libnn function optimization task.
- libnn-wiki-writer: Internal style guide for writing docs/wiki/ pages during /libnn-optimizer learn phase. Not a standalone skill -- read by the optimize agent.
- mlir-transform-writer: Write MLIR transform dialect scripts that directly control IR lowering - tiling, fusion, vectorization, bufferization, GPU thread mapping, shared memory promotion, and more. Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. Also trigger when the request involves composing IR transformations for linalg ops, controlling IREE codegen pipelines via transform dialect, or replacing annotation-only configs with full transform strategies. Covers both upstream MLIR transform ops and IREE-specific extensions.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- spec-human: Create a human-reviewable architecture spec using a 6-section template (Summary, Background, Architecture, Interface, Edge Cases, Alternatives) BEFORE implementing a non-trivial design. Triggered explicitly via /spec-human <topic>, or when the user says "write a human spec", "create a review-ready design doc", "spec this out for review", or "I need a spec for X before we build it". Produces an ASCII markdown document at ./specs/<slug>.md aimed at peer engineers and tech leads who need to validate core architecture and trade-offs in 5 minutes. Do NOT auto-trigger on general design questions or coding tasks - this is a deliberate review gate that only fires on explicit request. For LLM-targeted specs (future sibling skill), use /spec-llm instead.
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- ralph-loop:cancel-ralph: Cancel active Ralph Loop
- ralph-loop:help: Explain Ralph Loop plugin and available commands
- ralph-loop:ralph-loop: Start Ralph Loop in current session
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

aiTitle: 確認 Verilator 建置所需檔案

content.text:
`include/hybrid` 是 QEMU plugin、vsim、driver 三方共用的 ABI 合約。對「build verilator」來說，需要的是其中一部分:

| Header | vsim binary (`src/`) | vsim unit tests | 誰還在用 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `state_abi.h` | ✅ | ✅ | plugin, driver |
| `state_abi_check.h` | ✅ (被 `state_abi.h` 在 L117 include) | ✅ | plugin |
| `insn_match.h` | ✅ (`csr_trigger.hpp`, `handoff_controller.hpp`) | ✅ | plugin |
| `handoff_site.h` | ❌ | ✅ (只有 test) | plugin |
| `v_drain_policy.h` | ❌ | ✅ (只有 test) | plugin |
| `reg_names.h` | ❌ | ❌ | **只有** plugin |

- 只 build **vsim 執行檔** → 3 個: `state_abi.h` + `state_abi_check.h` + `insn_match.h`
- 連 **unit tests** 一起 build → 再加 `handoff_site.h`、`v_drain_policy.h`，共 5 個
- `reg_names.h` verilator 完全不用 (只有 QEMU plugin 用)

---

## 關於「移出 verilator」

先講現況: `verilator/` **已經是 submodule** 了 (`.gitmodules` → `hybrid_vsim`)。真正的問題是它的 build 反向往上抓 parent 的 header:

```
verilator/CMakeLists.txt:455
    "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/../include"   <- 伸手進 andesim 的 include/hybrid
```

submodule 往上抓 superproject 的檔案,是 git 的反模式 (anti-pattern)。所以 verilator **沒辦法單獨 build**。要乾淨地「移出」,就要切斷這條往上的線。

但 `include/hybrid` 不能直接搬進 verilator —— 因為 QEMU plugin (產生端) 和 driver 也要用它。把合約塞進「消費端」的 repo,等於讓生產者反過來依賴消費者,方向是錯的。

1	// Pattern recogniser for the magic handoff marker convention. The same
2	// predicate runs in two places: the QEMU TCG plugin (C) and the vsim PC
3	// pre-scan (C++).
4	//
5	// The markers are RISC-V HINT instructions: SLTI with rd=x0 discards its
6	// result, so it is an architectural NOP on every conforming core. Marker
7	// binaries therefore run unmodified on real silicon and on every engine
8	// (fast/cycle/hybrid) -- unlike the retired `csrwi 0x7C0` markers, where
9	// CSR 0x7C0 is MILMB on Andes cores and the exit marker enabled ILM at
10	// base 0, killing standalone runs. The 12-bit immediate carries the
11	// marker kind; rs1 is pinned to x0 so each marker is one exact 32-bit
12	// word. SLTI has no compressed form, so markers are always 4 bytes.
13	
14	#ifndef HYBRID_INSN_MATCH_H
15	#define HYBRID_INSN_MATCH_H
16	
17	#include <stdbool.h>
18	#include <stdint.h>
19	
20	#ifdef __cplusplus
21	extern "C" {
22	#endif
23	
24	typedef enum
25	{
26	  HYBRID_HANDOFF_NONE  = 0,
27	  HYBRID_HANDOFF_ENTER = 1,  // slti x0, x0, 0x5A0
28	  HYBRID_HANDOFF_EXIT  = 2,  // slti x0, x0, 0x5A1
29	} hybrid_handoff_kind;
30	
31	// slti x0, x0, imm: OP-IMM (0x13), funct3=010, rd=rs1=x0, imm[31:20].
32	#define HYBRID_MARKER_ENTER_INSN 0x5A002013u
33	#define HYBRID_MARKER_EXIT_INSN  0x5A102013u
34	
35	// Returns true when `insn` is one of the two marker HINTs. On match,
36	// *out_kind is set to ENTER or EXIT.
37	static inline bool hybrid_match_handoff_insn(uint32_t insn,
38	                                             hybrid_handoff_kind* out_kind)
39	{
40	  if (insn == HYBRID_MARKER_ENTER_INSN) {
41	    *out_kind = HYBRID_HANDOFF_ENTER;
42	    return true;
43	  }
44	  if (insn == HYBRID_MARKER_EXIT_INSN) {
45	    *out_kind = HYBRID_HANDOFF_EXIT;
46	    return true;
47	  }
48	  return false;
49	}
50	
51	#ifdef __cplusplus
52	}  // extern "C"
53	#endif
54	
55	#endif  // HYBRID_INSN_MATCH_H

/* B7: pure decision function for the QEMU plugin V-state drain gate.
 *
 * The plugin uses one `qemu_plugin_register*` handle per architectural V
 * register. Each handle is non-NULL iff the gdbstub feature XML
 * advertised that register at plugin init. The original gate at
 * hybrid_handoff.c:296 tested `if (v->vlenb && s.vlenb > 0)` which
 * silently omits the V block when:
 *   - vlenb was not advertised but vtype/vl were (partial V), or
 *   - vlenb was advertised but read as zero (V disabled at runtime).
 *
 * Mixing the "stub broke" case with the "V disabled" case loses
 * information; the partial-advertisement case should refuse rather than
 * pretend V is absent (the resume side then mis-restores).
 *
 * This header is pure C, no QEMU plugin dependency, so it can be unit-
 * tested from a host C++ doctest.
 */
#ifndef HYBRID_V_DRAIN_POLICY_H
#define HYBRID_V_DRAIN_POLICY_H

#include <stdint.h>

#include "hybrid/state_abi.h"  /* HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX: the L11 ceiling */

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

typedef enum {
    HYBRID_V_DRAIN_OK = 0,      /* proceed: copy full V block into state */
    HYBRID_V_DRAIN_SKIP = 1,    /* no V at all; do not set HYBRID_FLAG_V */
    HYBRID_V_DRAIN_ABORT = 2,   /* partial advertisement; refuse to drain */
} HybridVDrainPolicy;

/* Decide whether to drain the V block.
 *
 * has_vlenb:    1 iff the stub advertised the vlenb register handle.
 * has_other_v:  1 iff ANY of vtype/vl/vstart/vxsat/vxrm/vcsr/vreg[*] was
 *               advertised (i.e. some V state is visible).
 * vlenb_value:  the value read from vlenb (only meaningful when has_vlenb).
 */
static inline HybridVDrainPolicy
hybrid_v_drain_policy(int has_vlenb, int has_other_v, uint64_t vlenb_value)
{
    /* Truth table (see v_drain_policy.test.cpp):
     *   has_vlenb=0, has_other_v=0            -> SKIP   (no V)
     *   has_vlenb=0, has_other_v=1            -> ABORT  (partial advertisement)
     *   has_vlenb=1, has_other_v=0            -> SKIP   (nothing to drain)
     *   has_vlenb=1, has_other_v=1, vlenb=0   -> SKIP   (V disabled at runtime)
     *   has_vlenb=1, has_other_v=1, vlenb>MAX -> ABORT  (L11: wire format
     *                                            cannot hold this VLEN; never
     *                                            truncate silently)
     *   has_vlenb=1, has_other_v=1, otherwise -> OK
     */
    if (!has_vlenb && has_other_v) return HYBRID_V_DRAIN_ABORT;
    if (!has_other_v)              return HYBRID_V_DRAIN_SKIP;
    if (vlenb_value == 0)          return HYBRID_V_DRAIN_SKIP;
    if (vlenb_value > HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX) return HYBRID_V_DRAIN_ABORT;
    return HYBRID_V_DRAIN_OK;
}

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif

#endif  /* HYBRID_V_DRAIN_POLICY_H */

# andes-hybrid-abi

The shared wire-format contract for the Andes hybrid RISC-V simulator. These
headers define the bytes exchanged across the QEMU1 -> vsim handoff. They are
consumed by three independent components, so they live in their own repo and
are pinned as a submodule by each consumer (one source of truth, no drift):

| Consumer | Repo | Mounts this as |
|----------|------|----------------|
| `andesim` (QEMU TCG plugin + C++ driver) | top repo | `include/` |
| `hybrid_vsim` (vsim / SystemC + Verilator) | submodule | `external/hybrid-abi/` |

Both mount points put this repo's root on the include path, so every consumer
includes the same way:

```c
#include "hybrid/state_abi.h"
```

## Layout

```
hybrid/
  state_abi.h        struct hybrid_state_v1 -- the wire format
  state_abi_check.h  compile-time offset/size lock (static_assert)
  insn_match.h       handoff marker HINT recogniser
  handoff_site.h     translate-time trigger capture + post-trigger PC
  v_drain_policy.h   pure V-state drain gate decision
  reg_names.h        GDB register-name tables (gdbstub wire contract)
tests/
  abi_compile_check.{c,cpp}  include every header from C and C++
  check.sh                   compile both as C11 + C++20
```

## Contract rules

- Multi-byte fields are little-endian (native on RV64 + x86-64 host). Not
  endian-portable.
- Never repurpose offsets within a published version. Add fields by consuming
  bytes from `reserved`, or bump to v2. `state_abi_check.h` locks every offset;
  a layout change must update it in lock-step and bump `HYBRID_STATE_VERSION`.
- Both C and C++ must keep compiling these headers.

## Test

```sh
tests/check.sh        # host gcc/g++, zero external deps
```

A pass means the headers are self-contained from the repo root and the
`hybrid_state_v1` layout matches the locked offsets.

## History

Started fresh at the submodule split; the pre-split history of these headers
lives in the `andesim` repo under `include/hybrid/`.

# ROADMAP: split the shared ABI into its own repo, decouple verilator

## Goal

Make `verilator/` (the `hybrid_vsim` submodule) buildable on its own. Today its
CMake reaches UP into the parent at `../include` for the shared ABI headers --
a submodule depending on its superproject, the git anti-pattern. Extract
`include/hybrid/` into a standalone repo (`andes-hybrid-abi`) and pin it as a
submodule of BOTH `andesim` and `hybrid_vsim`. One source of truth; verilator
builds standalone.

## End state

```
andes-hybrid-abi/          NEW repo: root holds hybrid/<6 headers> + tests/
andesim/      (top repo)
  include/        -> submodule andes-hybrid-abi   (qemu_plugin + driver read here, unchanged paths)
  verilator/      -> submodule hybrid_vsim
       external/hybrid-abi -> submodule andes-hybrid-abi   (verilator reads here, builds alone)
  qemu_plugin/    HYBRID_INCLUDE ?= ../include    (unchanged)
  driver/         ../include                       (unchanged)
```

## Decisions (locked)

- ABI gets its OWN repo, submodule of both consumers (not vendored, not copied).
- Fresh git history (no filter-repo); pre-split history stays in andesim.
- `andesim/include/hybrid/*` include paths stay byte-identical -> ZERO source edits.
- Only build wiring changes: 2 verilator CMake lines + drop one Docker mount.
- User creates the empty Gitea repo; URL pending.

## Headers (the 6, who needs them)

- vsim binary needs: `state_abi.h` (+ `state_abi_check.h` transitively), `insn_match.h`
- vsim tests also need: `handoff_site.h`, `v_drain_policy.h`
- `reg_names.h`: only the QEMU plugin
- Moved as ONE unit (the whole `hybrid/` dir), not split.

## Features (one session each; update STATE as you go)

# ROADMAP: Andes HybridSim v1.0 (complete-all-features)

Single source of truth for everything required to ship Andes HybridSim
v1.0. Every feature traces to a functional requirement in `docs/FRS.md`,
which in turn traces to a market requirement in `docs/MRD.md`. Covering
all FRs therefore covers all MRs (FRS section 13 has no orphan).

This file **supersedes** two earlier engineering breakdowns, now in
`docs/archive/`:

- `docs/archive/commercial_v1_roadmap.md` - Waves 0-6 closing L1-L21
- `docs/archive/TODO.md` - failure-mode backlog F-T1.1..F-T3.8

Their content is absorbed below as full feature entries. `docs/andes_sim_limitations.ipynb`
stays as the plain-English "do not do this" envelope and the L-id source.

House rules (from `CLAUDE.md`): one session completes one feature. Update
the feature's Status when starting (in-progress) and on completion (done).
Each code feature carries a TDD RED line: the failing test you write first.

## Status legend

- not-started: no work yet
- in-progress: being implemented in a session
- partial: shipped for the M-mode envelope, incomplete for the full FR
- done: behavioural + structural commits landed, tests pass
- business: not a code task; a sign-off / process / legal deliverable

## Feature ID scheme

- `F-ENG-*` - engineering: ROI-envelope and correctness of the cycle engine
- `F-PROD-*` - productization: interfaces, trace, observability, encryption,
  licensing, packaging
- `F-BIZ-*` - business / legal / process: tagged `business`, no TDD RED

---

# ROADMAP: split the shared ABI into its own repo, decouple verilator

Scope: build-system restructuring only. Separate from the product
`ROADMAP.md` (the v1.0 FR tracker) -- this touches no FR, only git layout.

## Goal

Make `verilator/` (the `hybrid_vsim` submodule) buildable on its own. Today its
CMake reaches UP into the parent at `../include` for the shared ABI headers --
a submodule depending on its superproject, the git anti-pattern. Extract
`include/hybrid/` into a standalone repo (`andes-hybrid-abi`) and pin it as a
submodule of BOTH `andesim` and `hybrid_vsim`. One source of truth; verilator
builds standalone.

## End state

```
andes-hybrid-abi/          NEW repo: root holds hybrid/<6 headers> + tests/
andesim/      (top repo)
  include/        -> submodule andes-hybrid-abi   (qemu_plugin + driver read here, unchanged paths)
  verilator/      -> submodule hybrid_vsim
       external/hybrid-abi -> submodule andes-hybrid-abi   (verilator reads here, builds alone)
  qemu_plugin/    HYBRID_INCLUDE ?= ../include    (unchanged)
  driver/         ../include                       (unchanged)
```

## Decisions (locked)

- ABI gets its OWN repo, submodule of both consumers (not vendored, not copied).
- Fresh git history (no filter-repo); pre-split history stays in andesim.
- `andesim/include/hybrid/*` include paths stay byte-identical -> ZERO source edits.
- Only build wiring changes: 2 verilator CMake lines + drop one Docker mount.
- User creates the empty Gitea repo; URL pending.

## Headers (the 6, who needs them)

- vsim binary needs: `state_abi.h` (+ `state_abi_check.h` transitively), `insn_match.h`
- vsim tests also need: `handoff_site.h`, `v_drain_policy.h`
- `reg_names.h`: only the QEMU plugin
- Moved as ONE unit (the whole `hybrid/` dir), not split.

## Features (one session each; update STATE as you go)

### F1 -- create andes-hybrid-abi repo
- STATE: STAGED (content + self-test green in scratchpad; pending Gitea URL to push)
- Desc: new repo, root `hybrid/` = the 6 headers byte-exact, `tests/check.sh`
  compiles them as C11 + C++20 with the layout static_asserts firing, README.
- Verify: `tests/check.sh` -> "abi-compile-check OK" (passing in scratchpad now)
- Blocks on: Gitea URL (to set origin + push fresh initial commit)

### F2 -- andesim: include/ becomes a submodule
- STATE: TODO
- Desc: `git rm -r include` (the tracked dir), `git submodule add <url> include`.
- Key files: `.gitmodules`, `include/` (mode 160000)
- Verify: `make -C qemu_plugin` green; driver build green; headers identical.
- Depends on: F1 (needs the pushed repo URL)

### F3 -- verilator: external/hybrid-abi submodule + swap include paths
- STATE: TODO
- Desc: in the hybrid_vsim repo, `git submodule add <url> external/hybrid-abi`;
  change `../include` -> `external/hybrid-abi` in CMakeLists.txt:455 and
  cmake/HybridConfig.cmake:14; drop the `-v $ROOT/include:/include:ro` mount in
  andesim `scripts/build_vsim.sh` (headers now in-tree under /work/external).
- Key files: `verilator/.gitmodules`, `verilator/CMakeLists.txt`,
  `verilator/cmake/HybridConfig.cmake`, `scripts/build_vsim.sh`
- Verify: verilator builds STANDALONE (clone + submodule init + build, no parent
  include/ present) AND via `scripts/build_vsim.sh`.
- Depends on: F1

### F4 -- full-chain validation
- STATE: TODO
- Desc: bump verilator submodule pointer in andesim; build + test everything.
- Verify: `bash scripts/build_all.sh` green; `JOBS=8 bash scripts/run_e2e.sh`
  green; driver parity `tests/andes_sim/parity.sh` green; cycle figures
  unchanged vs a pre-split baseline.
- Depends on: F2, F3

### F5 -- publish
- STATE: TODO
- Desc: confirm Gitea URLs in both `.gitmodules`; push abi repo, push hybrid_vsim
  submodule bump, push andesim. Verify a fresh `git clone --recursive` builds.
- Verify: clean-clone `--recursive` -> `build_all.sh` green.
- Depends on: F4

## Notes

- Nested submodule: andes-hybrid-abi appears twice (andesim/include and
  andesim/verilator/external/hybrid-abi). Both pin the SAME commit; keep them in
  step when the ABI changes (bump abi -> bump in verilator -> bump verilator in
  andesim).
- `scripts/build_vsim.sh` currently mounts `$ROOT/include:/include:ro` so the
  container's `/work/../include` resolves. After F3 that mount is dead code.
- Staged F1 content lives in the session scratchpad until the URL arrives.

# andesim_abi

The shared wire-format contract for the Andes hybrid RISC-V simulator. These
headers define the bytes exchanged across the QEMU1 -> vsim handoff. They are
consumed by three independent components, so they live in their own repo and
are pinned as a submodule by each consumer (one source of truth, no drift):

| Consumer | Repo | Mounts this as |
|----------|------|----------------|
| `andesim` (QEMU TCG plugin + C++ driver) | top repo | `include/` |
| `hybrid_vsim` (vsim / SystemC + Verilator) | submodule | `external/andesim_abi/` |

Both mount points put this repo's root on the include path, so every consumer
includes the same way:

```c
#include "hybrid/state_abi.h"
```

## Layout

```
hybrid/
  state_abi.h        struct hybrid_state_v1 -- the wire format
  state_abi_check.h  compile-time offset/size lock (static_assert)
  insn_match.h       handoff marker HINT recogniser
  handoff_site.h     translate-time trigger capture + post-trigger PC
  v_drain_policy.h   pure V-state drain gate decision
  reg_names.h        GDB register-name tables (gdbstub wire contract)
tests/
  abi_compile_check.{c,cpp}  include every header from C and C++
  check.sh                   compile both as C11 + C++20
```

## Contract rules

- Multi-byte fields are little-endian (native on RV64 + x86-64 host). Not
  endian-portable.
- Never repurpose offsets within a published version. Add fields by consuming
  bytes from `reserved`, or bump to v2. `state_abi_check.h` locks every offset;
  a layout change must update it in lock-step and bump `HYBRID_STATE_VERSION`.
- Both C and C++ must keep compiling these headers.

## Test

```sh
tests/check.sh        # host gcc/g++, zero external deps
```

A pass means the headers are self-contained from the repo root and the
`hybrid_state_v1` layout matches the locked offsets.

## History

Started fresh at the submodule split; the pre-split history of these headers
lives in the `andesim` repo under `include/hybrid/`.

# ROADMAP: split the shared ABI into its own repo, decouple verilator

Scope: build-system restructuring only. Separate from the product
`ROADMAP.md` (the v1.0 FR tracker) -- this touches no FR, only git layout.

## Goal

Make `verilator/` (the `hybrid_vsim` submodule) buildable on its own. Today its
CMake reaches UP into the parent at `../include` for the shared ABI headers --
a submodule depending on its superproject, the git anti-pattern. Extract
`include/hybrid/` into a standalone repo (`andes-hybrid-abi`) and pin it as a
submodule of BOTH `andesim` and `hybrid_vsim`. One source of truth; verilator
builds standalone.

## End state

```
andes-hybrid-abi/          NEW repo: root holds hybrid/<6 headers> + tests/
andesim/      (top repo)
  include/        -> submodule andes-hybrid-abi   (qemu_plugin + driver read here, unchanged paths)
  verilator/      -> submodule hybrid_vsim
       external/andesim_abi -> submodule andes-hybrid-abi   (verilator reads here, builds alone)
  qemu_plugin/    HYBRID_INCLUDE ?= ../include    (unchanged)
  driver/         ../include                       (unchanged)
```

## Decisions (locked)

- ABI gets its OWN repo, submodule of both consumers (not vendored, not copied).
- Fresh git history (no filter-repo); pre-split history stays in andesim.
- `andesim/include/hybrid/*` include paths stay byte-identical -> ZERO source edits.
- Only build wiring changes: 2 verilator CMake lines + drop one Docker mount.
- User creates the empty Gitea repo; URL pending.

## Headers (the 6, who needs them)

- vsim binary needs: `state_abi.h` (+ `state_abi_check.h` transitively), `insn_match.h`
- vsim tests also need: `handoff_site.h`, `v_drain_policy.h`
- `reg_names.h`: only the QEMU plugin
- Moved as ONE unit (the whole `hybrid/` dir), not split.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build vsim inside the env-stage container image.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
VSIM_DIR="$ROOT/verilator"

if [[ ! -f "$VSIM_DIR/Dockerfile" ]]; then
  echo "missing $VSIM_DIR/Dockerfile - run 'git submodule update --init --recursive'" >&2
  exit 1
fi

cd "$VSIM_DIR"

podman build --target env -t vsim-env:latest .
podman run --rm \
  -v "$PWD:/work" \
  -v "$ROOT/include:/include:ro" \
  -w /work localhost/vsim-env:latest ./build.sh

# ROADMAP: split the shared ABI into its own repo, decouple verilator

Scope: build-system restructuring only. Separate from the product
`ROADMAP.md` (the v1.0 FR tracker) -- this touches no FR, only git layout.

## Goal

Make `verilator/` (the `hybrid_vsim` submodule) buildable on its own. Today its
CMake reaches UP into the parent at `../include` for the shared ABI headers --
a submodule depending on its superproject, the git anti-pattern. Extract
`include/hybrid/` into a standalone repo (`andesim_abi`) and pin it as a
submodule of BOTH `andesim` and `hybrid_vsim`. One source of truth; verilator
builds standalone.

## End state

```
andesim_abi/          NEW repo: root holds hybrid/<6 headers> + tests/
andesim/      (top repo)
  include/        -> submodule andesim_abi   (qemu_plugin + driver read here, unchanged paths)
  verilator/      -> submodule hybrid_vsim
       external/andesim_abi -> submodule andesim_abi   (verilator reads here, builds alone)
  qemu_plugin/    HYBRID_INCLUDE ?= ../include    (unchanged)
  driver/         ../include                       (unchanged)
```

## Decisions (locked)

- ABI gets its OWN repo, submodule of both consumers (not vendored, not copied).
- Fresh git history (no filter-repo); pre-split history stays in andesim.
- `andesim/include/hybrid/*` include paths stay byte-identical -> ZERO source edits.
- Only build wiring changes: 2 verilator CMake lines + drop one Docker mount.
- User creates the empty Gitea repo; URL pending.

- vsim binary needs: `state_abi.h` (+ `state_abi_check.h` transitively), `insn_match.h`
- vsim tests also need: `handoff_site.h`, `v_drain_policy.h`
- `reg_names.h`: only the QEMU plugin
- Moved as ONE unit (the whole `hybrid/` dir), not split.

## Goal

Make `verilator/` (the `hybrid_vsim` submodule) buildable on its own. Today its

a submodule depending on its superproject, the git anti-pattern. Extract

# ROADMAP: split the shared ABI into its own repo, decouple verilator

Scope: build-system restructuring only. Separate from the product
`ROADMAP.md` (the v1.0 FR tracker) -- this touches no FR, only git layout.

## Goal

Make `verilator/` (the `hybrid_vsim` submodule) buildable on its own. Today its
CMake reaches UP into the parent at `../include` for the shared ABI headers --
a submodule depending on its superproject, the git anti-pattern. Extract
`include/hybrid/` into a standalone repo (`andesim_abi`) and pin it as a
submodule of BOTH `andesim` and `hybrid_vsim`. One source of truth; verilator
builds standalone.

## End state

```
andesim_abi/          NEW repo: root holds hybrid/<6 headers> + tests/
andesim/      (top repo)
  include/        -> submodule andesim_abi   (qemu_plugin + driver read here, unchanged paths)
  verilator/      -> submodule hybrid_vsim
       external/andesim_abi -> submodule andesim_abi   (verilator reads here, builds alone)
  qemu_plugin/    HYBRID_INCLUDE ?= ../include    (unchanged)
  driver/         ../include                       (unchanged)
```

## Decisions (locked)

- ABI gets its OWN repo, submodule of both consumers (not vendored, not copied).
- Fresh git history (no filter-repo); pre-split history stays in andesim.
- `andesim/include/hybrid/*` include paths stay byte-identical -> ZERO source edits.
- Only build wiring changes: 2 verilator CMake lines + drop one Docker mount.
- User creates the empty Gitea repo; URL pending.

## Headers (the 6, who needs them)

- vsim binary needs: `state_abi.h` (+ `state_abi_check.h` transitively), `insn_match.h`
- vsim tests also need: `handoff_site.h`, `v_drain_policy.h`
- `reg_names.h`: only the QEMU plugin
- Moved as ONE unit (the whole `hybrid/` dir), not split.

## Features (one session each; update STATE as you go)

### F1 -- create andesim_abi repo
- STATE: DONE (pushed to gitea.andestech.com/nick/andesim_abi, branch main, commit d9c5d9b)
- Desc: new repo, root `hybrid/` = the 6 headers byte-exact, `tests/check.sh`
  compiles them as C11 + C++20 with the layout static_asserts firing, README.
- Verify: `tests/check.sh` -> "abi-compile-check OK" (passing in scratchpad now)
- Blocks on: Gitea URL (to set origin + push fresh initial commit)

### F2 -- andesim: include/ becomes a submodule
- STATE: DONE (andesim commit 8d77d1a; qemu_plugin builds 2 .so + driver ABI TUs compile)
- Desc: `git rm -r include` (the tracked dir), `git submodule add <url> include`.
- Key files: `.gitmodules`, `include/` (mode 160000)
- Verify: `make -C qemu_plugin` green; driver build green; headers identical.
- Depends on: F1 (needs the pushed repo URL)

### F3 -- verilator: external/andesim_abi submodule + swap include paths
- STATE: DONE (verilator commit 619db38 on branch andesim; andesim build_vsim.sh
  commit 3ea60d6; all 8 hybrid headers resolve the ABI via the new path)
- Desc: in the hybrid_vsim repo, `git submodule add <url> external/andesim_abi`;
  change `../include` -> `external/andesim_abi` in CMakeLists.txt:455 and
  cmake/HybridConfig.cmake:14; drop the `-v $ROOT/include:/include:ro` mount in
  andesim `scripts/build_vsim.sh` (headers now in-tree under /work/external).
- Key files: `verilator/.gitmodules`, `verilator/CMakeLists.txt`,
  `verilator/cmake/HybridConfig.cmake`, `scripts/build_vsim.sh`

## Notes

input.content:
# ROADMAP: externalize verilator (drop the submodule, mirror the QEMU pattern)

Follows the same move already done for QEMU (commits "drop the QEMU submodule,
integrate a prebuilt external QEMU" + "set QEMU_BIN_DIR"). andesim stops nesting
verilator as a submodule; it consumes a prebuilt vsim from an external location
(e.g. `/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/build`) via `VSIM_BIN_DIR`, exactly like
`QEMU_BIN_DIR` points at the external qemu.

## Why / end state

```
BEFORE:  andesim/verilator  (submodule, andesim builds + records it)
AFTER:   andesim            (no verilator submodule)
         vsim_andesim/      (external sibling repo = hybrid_vsim; built there)
         config.env: VSIM_BIN_DIR=/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/build   <- new, mirrors QEMU_BIN_DIR
```

## Relationship to the abi-split work (already done)

- KEEP: F1 (andesim_abi repo) + F2 (andesim include/ submodule). qemu_plugin and
  the driver still consume the ABI from include/.
- KEEP in hybrid_vsim: F3 (external/andesim_abi submodule + CMake swap). vsim_andesim
  needs it to build standalone. Must reach hybrid_vsim origin (see EX5).
- REVERT: F4's andesim verilator-pointer bump (commit 815259d). With no submodule,
  andesim records no verilator commit. EX3 removes the gitlink entirely.

## Safety gate (before EX3, the destructive step)

`619db38` (the F3 ABI-split commit) is only in local checkouts (andesim/verilator
branch andesim; vsim_andesim branch abi-split-verify), NOT on origin. Before
deleting andesim/verilator, push the F3 work to hybrid_vsim origin's `andesim`
branch so vsim_andesim (and any clone) is reproducible. After that, deleting the
local andesim/verilator loses nothing.

## env-var design (mirror QEMU exactly)

| External thing | env (config.env) | setup.sh exports | driver reads |
|----------------|------------------|------------------|--------------|
| qemu           | `QEMU_BIN_DIR`   | `VSIM_QEMU`      | builtin_qemu path |
| vsim (NEW)     | `VSIM_BIN_DIR`   | `VSIM_BIN_DIR` (+ `ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR`) | engine scan dir |

Driver already has `ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR` (scan any executable). New: an explicit
`VSIM_BIN_DIR` seam that keeps the `sim_` prefix, falling back to the old
`<repo>/verilator/build` when unset (dev back-compat until the submodule is gone).

## Features (one session each; TDD on the driver C++)

### EX1 -- driver: discover engines from VSIM_BIN_DIR
- STATE: TODO
- Type: behavioural
- Desc: add a pure `vsim_scan_dir()` seam: `VSIM_BIN_DIR` if set, else
  `repo_root()/verilator/build`. `discover_engines()` and `cmd_doctor` use it.
  Drop cmd_doctor's `verilator/CMakeLists.txt` submodule-presence check.
- Key files: `driver/engine_registry.cpp`, `driver/cmd_doctor.cpp`,
  `driver/engine_registry_test.cpp` (new)
- TDD RED: `vsim_scan_dir()` returns `$VSIM_BIN_DIR` when the env is set; today no
  such function exists / discover_engines hardcodes verilator/build.
- Verify: new doctest green; `andesim-plan-itest` still green.
- Non-destructive (fallback preserved).

### EX2 -- setup.sh + config.env.example: external VSIM_BIN_DIR
- STATE: TODO
- Desc: config.env.example gains `VSIM_BIN_DIR=` (mirrors QEMU_BIN_DIR). setup.sh
  reads it from config.env instead of hardcoding `$ROOT/verilator/build`,
  validates a `sim_*` exists (like the qemu-system check), exports `VSIM_BIN_DIR`
  + `ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR` for the driver and e2e scripts, and drops the vsim
  BUILD steps.
- Key files: `config.env.example`, `setup.sh`
- Verify: `source ./setup.sh` with VSIM_BIN_DIR=vsim_andesim/build, then
  `./andesim list engines` lists the external vsim engines.
- Depends on: EX1

### EX3 -- remove the verilator submodule (DESTRUCTIVE; gated)
- STATE: TODO
- Desc: revert the F4 pointer bump; `git rm verilator`; drop the `.gitmodules`
  entry; `rm -rf .git/modules/verilator`; remove `scripts/build_vsim.sh`; update
  `scripts/build_all.sh` (drop the vsim build leg); resolve `Dockerfile.runtime`
  (it does `cd verilator && ./build.sh` -- repoint at the external vsim image or
  drop that stage); fix `tests/vplat/test_vplat_f8.sh` to use VSIM_BIN_DIR.
- Key files: `.gitmodules`, `verilator` (gitlink), `scripts/build_all.sh`,
  `scripts/build_vsim.sh`, `Dockerfile.runtime`, `tests/vplat/test_vplat_f8.sh`,
  `hsim.py` (retired golden -- decide: update or leave frozen)
- Verify: andesim has no verilator/ submodule; `build_all.sh` + `./andesim run`
  work against the external vsim.
- Depends on: EX2 + the safety gate (F3 pushed to hybrid_vsim origin)

### EX4 -- docs
- STATE: TODO
- Desc: USER_GUIDE.md, CLAUDE.md, docs/engine_interface.md, README reflect the
  external vsim (build at vsim_andesim, set VSIM_BIN_DIR) and the removed submodule.
- Depends on: EX3

### EX5 -- publish
- STATE: TODO
- Desc: push hybrid_vsim `andesim` branch (the F3 ABI-split, =619db38 content) to
  origin; push andesim_abi (already done F1); push andesim externalization commits.
  Verify a fresh `git clone --recursive andesim` + external vsim build works.
- Depends on: EX4

## Notes

- Engine TYPE label "verilator" (driver/engine_descriptor, json, docs) is the
  engine FAMILY name, normalized to "vsim" for users. It is NOT the submodule
  path and stays unchanged.
- The driver's `repo_root()/build/qemu/...` for builtin qemu is separate; this

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Driver: build vsim + plugin (qemu is external), then add build dirs to PATH.
# Source this script to affect your current shell's PATH:
#   source ./setup.sh                       # build all
#   source ./setup.sh clean [target]        # clean vsim|plugin|all (default: all)

if [ -n "${ZSH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
  _SETUP_SRC="${(%):-%x}"
elif [ -n "${BASH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
  _SETUP_SRC="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
else
  _SETUP_SRC="$0"
fi

# Wrap the body in a function so strict-mode options stay local and don't
# leak into the caller's interactive shell (which would break zsh prompts
# under nounset).
_hybrid_setup_main() {
  if [ -n "${ZSH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
    emulate -L sh
    setopt err_exit no_unset pipe_fail
  else
    local -
    set -euo pipefail
  fi

  local ROOT QEMU_BIN_DIR VSIM_BIN_DIR PLUGIN_DIR PLUGIN_SO CONFIG_FILE CONFIG_TEMPLATE
  ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$_SETUP_SRC")" && pwd)"
  # QEMU_BIN_DIR (the externally-built qemu-system-* directory) comes from
  # config.env -- this project integrates a prebuilt QEMU, it no longer builds one.
  VSIM_BIN_DIR="$ROOT/verilator/build"
  PLUGIN_DIR="$ROOT/qemu_plugin"
  PLUGIN_SO="$PLUGIN_DIR/libhybrid_handoff.so"
  CONFIG_FILE="$ROOT/config.env"
  CONFIG_TEMPLATE="$ROOT/config.env.example"

  step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m \033[1m%s\033[0m\n' "$*"; }
  ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
  err()  { printf '\033[1;31m[err]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }

  clean_vsim()   { step "cleaning vsim build ($VSIM_BIN_DIR)";   rm -rf "$VSIM_BIN_DIR"; ok "vsim cleaned"; }
  clean_plugin() {
    step "cleaning plugin build ($PLUGIN_DIR)"
    if [ -f "$PLUGIN_DIR/Makefile" ]; then
      make -C "$PLUGIN_DIR" clean
    else
      rm -f "$PLUGIN_SO" "$PLUGIN_DIR"/*.o
    fi
    ok "plugin cleaned"
  }

  if [ "${1:-}" = "clean" ]; then
    case "${2:-all}" in
      vsim)     clean_vsim ;;
      plugin)   clean_plugin ;;
      all)      clean_vsim; clean_plugin ;;
      *)        err "usage: source $_SETUP_SRC clean [vsim|plugin|all]"; return 1 ;;
    esac
    return 0
  fi

  step "0/3 loading per-host config"
  if [ ! -f "$CONFIG_FILE" ]; then
    if [ ! -f "$CONFIG_TEMPLATE" ]; then
      err "missing $CONFIG_TEMPLATE; cannot create $CONFIG_FILE"
      return 1
    fi
    cp "$CONFIG_TEMPLATE" "$CONFIG_FILE"
    ok "created $CONFIG_FILE from template -- edit it if your toolchain lives elsewhere"
  fi
  # shellcheck source=/dev/null
  . "$CONFIG_FILE"
  if [ -z "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}" ]; then
    err "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN not set; check $CONFIG_FILE"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ ! -d "$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin" ]; then
    err "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN has no bin/ directory; edit $CONFIG_FILE"
    return 1
  fi
  export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN
  ok "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN"

  step "1/3 locating external qemu"
  if [ -z "${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-}" ]; then
    err "QEMU_BIN_DIR not set; point it at your qemu-system-* build dir in $CONFIG_FILE"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ ! -x "$QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-riscv64" ]; then
    err "no qemu-system-riscv64 under QEMU_BIN_DIR=$QEMU_BIN_DIR; build QEMU there or edit $CONFIG_FILE"
    return 1
  fi
  ok "qemu <- $QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-riscv64 (external, prebuilt)"

  step "2/3 building vsim"
  "$ROOT/scripts/build_vsim.sh"
  ok "vsim -> $VSIM_BIN_DIR/vsim"

  step "3/3 building hybrid plugin"
  if [ ! -f "$PLUGIN_DIR/Makefile" ]; then
    err "missing $PLUGIN_DIR/Makefile"
    return 1
  fi
  # Plugins build against the vendored qemu_plugin/include/qemu-plugin.h -- no
  # QEMU source tree required.
  make -C "$PLUGIN_DIR"
  ok "plugin -> $PLUGIN_SO"

  step "PATH: prepending build dirs"
  case ":$PATH:" in
    *":$QEMU_BIN_DIR:"*) ;;
    *) export PATH="$QEMU_BIN_DIR:$PATH" ;;
  esac
  case ":$PATH:" in
    *":$VSIM_BIN_DIR:"*) ;;
    *) export PATH="$VSIM_BIN_DIR:$PATH" ;;
  esac
  ok "PATH updated (this shell only)"

  step "env: exporting QEMU_BIN_DIR / VSIM_QEMU / VSIM_PLUGIN for e2e scripts"
  export QEMU_BIN_DIR
  export VSIM_QEMU="$QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-riscv64"
  export VSIM_PLUGIN="$PLUGIN_SO"
  ok "QEMU_BIN_DIR=$QEMU_BIN_DIR"
  ok "VSIM_QEMU=$VSIM_QEMU"
  ok "VSIM_PLUGIN=$VSIM_PLUGIN"

  if [ -n "${BASH_VERSION:-}" ] && [ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]:-}" = "${0:-}" ]; then
    err "script was executed, not sourced - PATH change is local to this subshell"
    err "to update your shell, run: source $_SETUP_SRC"
  fi
}

_hybrid_setup_main "$@"
unset -f _hybrid_setup_main 2>/dev/null
unset _SETUP_SRC

  _SETUP_SRC="${(%):-%x}"
elif [ -n "${BASH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
  _SETUP_SRC="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
else
  _SETUP_SRC="$0"
fi

# Wrap the body in a function so strict-mode options stay local and don't
# leak into the caller's interactive shell (which would break zsh prompts
# under nounset).
_hybrid_setup_main() {
  if [ -n "${ZSH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
    emulate -L sh
    setopt err_exit no_unset pipe_fail
  else
    local -
    set -euo pipefail
  fi

  local ROOT QEMU_BIN_DIR VSIM_BIN_DIR PLUGIN_DIR PLUGIN_SO CONFIG_FILE CONFIG_TEMPLATE
  ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$_SETUP_SRC")" && pwd)"
  # QEMU_BIN_DIR (the externally-built qemu-system-* directory) comes from
  # config.env -- this project integrates a prebuilt QEMU, it no longer builds one.
  VSIM_BIN_DIR="$ROOT/verilator/build"
  PLUGIN_DIR="$ROOT/qemu_plugin"
  PLUGIN_SO="$PLUGIN_DIR/libhybrid_handoff.so"
  CONFIG_FILE="$ROOT/config.env"
  CONFIG_TEMPLATE="$ROOT/config.env.example"

  step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m \033[1m%s\033[0m\n' "$*"; }
  ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
  err()  { printf '\033[1;31m[err]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }

  clean_vsim()   { step "cleaning vsim build ($VSIM_BIN_DIR)";   rm -rf "$VSIM_BIN_DIR"; ok "vsim cleaned"; }
  clean_plugin() {
    step "cleaning plugin build ($PLUGIN_DIR)"
    if [ -f "$PLUGIN_DIR/Makefile" ]; then
      make -C "$PLUGIN_DIR" clean
    else
      rm -f "$PLUGIN_SO" "$PLUGIN_DIR"/*.o
    fi
    ok "plugin cleaned"
  }

  if [ "${1:-}" = "clean" ]; then
    case "${2:-all}" in
      vsim)     clean_vsim ;;
      plugin)   clean_plugin ;;
      all)      clean_vsim; clean_plugin ;;

    err "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN not set; check $CONFIG_FILE"
    return 1

    err "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN has no bin/ directory; edit $CONFIG_FILE"
    return 1

  ok "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN"

  "$ROOT/scripts/build_vsim.sh"
  ok "vsim -> $VSIM_BIN_DIR/vsim"

    err "missing $PLUGIN_DIR/Makefile"
    return 1

  case ":$PATH:" in

  esac

    *":$VSIM_BIN_DIR:"*) ;;
    *) export PATH="$VSIM_BIN_DIR:$PATH" ;;
  esac

  export QEMU_BIN_DIR

  ok "VSIM_QEMU=$VSIM_QEMU"
  ok "VSIM_PLUGIN=$VSIM_PLUGIN"

    err "script was executed, not sourced - PATH change is local to this subshell"
    err "to update your shell, run: source $_SETUP_SRC"
  fi
}

_hybrid_setup_main "$@"

unset _SETUP_SRC

  clean_vsim()   { step "vsim is external (${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-unset})"; ok "not cleaned here -- clean it in your external vsim checkout"; }

    esac

  ok "QEMU_BIN_DIR=$QEMU_BIN_DIR"
  ok "VSIM_QEMU=$VSIM_QEMU"
  ok "VSIM_PLUGIN=$VSIM_PLUGIN"

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
VSIM_DIR="$ROOT/verilator"
HARNESS="$ROOT/tests"
TEST_DIR="$ROOT/tests/fixtures"

VSIM_QEMU="${VSIM_QEMU:-$ROOT/build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64}"
VSIM_PLUGIN="${VSIM_PLUGIN:-$ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so}"
if [[ -z "${VSIM_BIN:-}" ]]; then
  # Default to the repo's canonical SINGLE-HART engine (the same one ./andesim
  # pins). The fixtures are single-hart programs: on a multicore build like
  # sim_ax45mpv_mp2 -- which sorts FIRST under verilator/build/ -- the
  # secondary hart runs crt0 from reset, writes SKIPPED to SimControl and
  # stops the sim before hart 0 drains, failing every C fixture. Fall back
  # to the first sim_* only when the canonical engine is not built.
  VSIM_BIN="$VSIM_DIR/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
  if [[ ! -x "$VSIM_BIN" ]]; then
    VSIM_BIN=$(ls "$VSIM_DIR"/build/sim_* 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)
  fi
fi

step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }

   1 #!/usr/bin/env bash
   2 # build_all.sh -- build the andesim artifacts. This is the entry point that
   3 # replaced the former `andesim build` subcommand (which moved out of the driver
   4 # binary). It only orchestrates the existing build scripts / Makefiles; the
   5 # build logic itself lives in setup.sh, scripts/build_*.sh, and the Makefiles.
   6 #
   7 # Usage:
   8 #   scripts/build_all.sh [TARGET] [--dry-run]
   9 #
  10 # TARGET (default: all):
  11 #   all       setup.sh (locate external qemu + vsim + plugin) then
  12 #             fixtures (the fixtures Makefile also builds the runtime lib too)
  13 #   vsim      verilator/build/sim_*
  14 #   plugin    qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so
  15 #   fixtures  tests/fixtures/*.elf (+ runtime lib)
  16 #   runtime   build/runtime/ (libandesim_runtime.a, crt0.o, andesim.ld, andesim.specs)
  17 #
  18 # --dry-run prints the underlying commands without running them.
  19 #
  20 # The andesim driver itself is NOT built here: ./andesim self-bootstraps via
  21 # scripts/build_driver.sh on first use.
  22 set -euo pipefail
  23 
  24 ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
  25 
  26 TARGET=all
  27 DRY_RUN=0
  28 for arg in "$@"; do
  29   case "$arg" in
  30     --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1 ;;
  31     all|vsim|plugin|fixtures|runtime) TARGET="$arg" ;;
  32     *)
  33       echo "build_all.sh: unknown argument: $arg" >&2
  34       echo "usage: build_all.sh [all|vsim|plugin|fixtures|runtime] [--dry-run]" >&2
  35       exit 2
  36       ;;
  37   esac
  38 done
  39 
  40 # run one step: print it under --dry-run, otherwise banner + execute (inheriting
  41 # stdio so the user watches the build live). set -e aborts on the first failure.
  42 run() {
  43   if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
  44     printf '%s\n' "$*"
  45     return
  46   fi
  47   printf '[build_all] %s\n' "$*"
  48   "$@"
  49 }
  50 
  51 # plugin: build_qemu_plugin.sh wraps `make -C qemu_plugin`; plugins build against

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Runtime-lib F3 contract: the whole link recipe collapses into two flags --
#
#   gcc -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 \
#       -B <repo>/build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs hello.c -o hello.elf
#
# The specs file swaps the startfile to our crt0.o, appends -T andesim.ld
# and rewrites the library sequence to
# `--start-group -landesim_runtime -lc -lgcc --end-group` (no -lgloss,
# no semihosting). The produced ELF must run on all three engines.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. "$ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null
export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:?config.env missing}"
GCC="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
SIM="$ROOT/verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
RT="$ROOT/build/runtime"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "driver not built: $BIN"
[ -x "$SIM" ] || fail "cycle engine not built: $SIM"
[ -x "$ROOT/build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64" ] || fail "qemu not built"
[ -f "$ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so" ] || fail "plugin not built"

make -C "$ROOT/runtime" >/dev/null || fail "runtime lib build failed"

TMP=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
cat > "$TMP/hello.c" <<'EOF'
#include <stdio.h>

__attribute__((noinline)) void say_hello(void)
{
  printf("hello from specs\n");
}

int main(void)
{
  say_hello();
  __asm__ __volatile__(".globl vplat_roi_end\nvplat_roi_end:" ::: "memory");
  return 0;
}
EOF

# The two-flag user command (plus a link map for the no-gloss assert).
"$GCC" -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 \
  -B "$RT" -specs=andesim.specs "$TMP/hello.c" -o "$TMP/hello.elf" \
  -Wl,-Map,"$TMP/hello.map" || fail "two-flag specs link failed"

grep 'libandesim_runtime\.a' "$TMP/hello.map" >/dev/null \
  || fail "link map does not pull libandesim_runtime.a"
if grep 'gloss' "$TMP/hello.map" >/dev/null; then
  fail "link map pulls a libgloss (semihosting leaked into the link)"
fi

# cycle
OUT=$(timeout 120 "$SIM" "$TMP/hello.elf" </dev/null 2>&1); RC=$?
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q 'hello from specs' \
  || fail "cycle: missing 'hello from specs' in: $OUT"
[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "cycle: exit code $RC != 0 (output: $OUT)"

# fast
OUT=$(timeout 60 "$BIN" run --mode fast "$TMP/hello.elf" </dev/null 2>&1); RC=$?
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q 'hello from specs' \
  || fail "fast: missing 'hello from specs' in: $OUT"
[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "fast: exit code $RC != 0 (output: $OUT)"

# hybrid (pc trigger on the same symbols a user would publish)
OUT=$(timeout 180 "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger pc \
        --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium \
        --pc-start say_hello --pc-end vplat_roi_end \
        "$TMP/hello.elf" </dev/null 2>&1)
RC=$?
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q 'hello from specs' \
  || fail "hybrid: missing 'hello from specs' in: $OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -Eq '^\[pc window_cycles\] [0-9]+' \
  || fail "hybrid: missing window_cycles line: $OUT"
[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "hybrid: exit code $RC != 0 (output: $OUT)"

ok "F3 -specs=andesim.specs builds one ELF that runs on fast, cycle, hybrid"

# andesim runtime image -- for run-only hosts (macOS via podman machine).
#
# Built ON LINUX (CI or a Linux workstation); macOS users only pull it:
#
#   podman build -f Dockerfile.runtime \
#     --build-arg BASE_IMAGE=<verilator env image> \
#     -t andesim-runtime:latest .
#
# BASE_IMAGE is the vsim build environment from verilator/Dockerfile
# (target `env`) -- the same image scripts/build_vsim.sh uses, so the
# Verilator/SystemC toolchain and QEMU build deps are already there.
# The publish registry/name is still an open question; consumers override
# the local default with ANDESIM_IMAGE.
#
# The whole repo is baked, fully built, at /opt/hybrid_sim, so the baked
# ./andesim resolves every artifact via its normal repo-relative paths
# (build/qemu, engines, plugin, runtime). scripts/run_in_container.sh
# invokes that path as the entry; the user's cwd is bind-mounted only for
# ELF inputs and outputs.
ARG BASE_IMAGE=andes-vsim-env:latest
FROM ${BASE_IMAGE}

COPY . /opt/hybrid_sim
WORKDIR /opt/hybrid_sim

# Build: vsim -> plugin -> driver -> runtime. QEMU is NOT built here -- it is
# integrated as an external prebuilt binary; provide it at run time, e.g.
#   -v /path/to/qemu/build:/qemu:ro -e VSIM_QEMU=/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64
# (the plugin builds against the vendored qemu_plugin/include/qemu-plugin.h, so
# no QEMU source tree is needed). setup.sh is NOT used because its vsim stage
# (scripts/build_vsim.sh) spawns podman; here we already ARE in the vsim env
# image, so verilator/build.sh runs directly.
RUN (cd verilator && ./build.sh) \
 && make -C qemu_plugin \
 && ./scripts/build_driver.sh \
 && make -C runtime

ENTRYPOINT ["/opt/hybrid_sim/andesim"]

# Shared path resolution for the top-level e2e harness + drivers.
# Sourced (not executed). Provides:
#   TOP_ROOT                  - absolute path of the repo root
#   hybrid_resolve_paths()    - sets VSIM_BIN, VSIM_QEMU, VSIM_PLUGIN,
#                               VSIM_ELF from TOP_ROOT (unless already
#                               exported by caller) and exits 77 (CTest
#                               skip) if any artifact is missing. Reads
#                               FIXTURE for the VSIM_ELF default.

TESTS_LIB_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
TOP_ROOT=$(cd -- "$TESTS_LIB_DIR/../.." && pwd)

if [ -z "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}" ] && [ -f "$TOP_ROOT/config.env" ]; then
  . "$TOP_ROOT/config.env"
fi

hybrid_resolve_paths() {
  VSIM_BIN="${VSIM_BIN:-$TOP_ROOT/verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium}"
  VSIM_QEMU="${VSIM_QEMU:-${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-$TOP_ROOT/build/qemu}/qemu-system-riscv64}"
  VSIM_PLUGIN="${VSIM_PLUGIN:-$TOP_ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so}"
  VSIM_ELF="${VSIM_ELF:-$TOP_ROOT/tests/fixtures/${FIXTURE}.elf}"
  for f in "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_QEMU" "$VSIM_PLUGIN" "$VSIM_ELF"; do
    if [ ! -e "$f" ]; then
      echo "skip: $f not built; run 'source ./setup.sh' and 'make -C tests/fixtures'"
      exit 77
    fi
  done
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Runtime-lib F2 contract: `make -C runtime` produces a linkable library
# under build/runtime/ so users stop listing the 4 runtime sources:
#
#   build/runtime/libandesim_runtime.a   (trap.o handler.o vplat_syscalls.o)
#   build/runtime/crt0.o                   (startfile; OUTSIDE the archive)
#   build/runtime/andesim.ld             (linker script)
#
# Probe: link vplat_hello.c with the raw library line (no specs file yet)
# and run it on the cycle engine -- prints via UART, exits 0 via SimControl.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. "$ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null
export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:?config.env missing}"
GCC="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc"
NM="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm"

SIM="$ROOT/verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
[ -x "$SIM" ] || fail "cycle engine not built: $SIM"

make -C "$ROOT/runtime" || fail "runtime lib build failed"

RT="$ROOT/build/runtime"
[ -f "$RT/libandesim_runtime.a" ] || fail "missing $RT/libandesim_runtime.a"
[ -f "$RT/crt0.o" ] || fail "missing $RT/crt0.o"
[ -f "$RT/andesim.ld" ] || fail "missing $RT/andesim.ld"

# crt0 must be a standalone startfile: the archive never gets _start pulled.
# (grep without -q: early-exit + pipefail turns a MATCH into SIGPIPE failure)
"$NM" "$RT/crt0.o" | grep ' T _start' >/dev/null \
  || fail "crt0.o does not define _start"
"$NM" "$RT/libandesim_runtime.a" | grep ' T _write' >/dev/null \
  || fail "archive does not define _write"
"$NM" "$RT/libandesim_runtime.a" | grep ' T m_trap_entry' >/dev/null \
  || fail "archive does not define m_trap_entry"

# Raw (non-specs) link: what a non-gcc-driver build system would write.
TMP=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
"$GCC" -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -static -nostartfiles -nodefaultlibs \
  -T "$RT/andesim.ld" "$RT/crt0.o" "$ROOT/tests/fixtures/vplat_hello.c" \
  -L "$RT" -Wl,--start-group -landesim_runtime -lc -lgcc -Wl,--end-group \
  -o "$TMP/hello.elf" || fail "raw -landesim_runtime link failed"

OUT=$(timeout 120 "$SIM" "$TMP/hello.elf" </dev/null 2>&1); RC=$?
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q 'hello from vplat' \
  || fail "cycle: missing 'hello from vplat' in: $OUT"
[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "cycle: exit code $RC != 0 (output: $OUT)"

ok "F2 libandesim_runtime.a links and runs on the cycle engine"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# RED test for F4: `./hsim.py test [--filter REGEX] [--mode marker|pc|both] [--jobs N]`.
#
# Wraps scripts/run_e2e.sh with JOBS=8 default; parses results.tsv and
# prints a `PASS X, FAIL Y, SKIP Z` summary. Parameter resolution is
# verified via `--dry-run` (same pattern as F2's build subcommand).
# The real smoke step at the end is gated on built artifacts.

set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
HSIM="$ROOT/hsim.py"

. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

[ -x "$HSIM" ] || fail "missing executable: $HSIM"

# 1. --help mentions --filter, --mode, --jobs.
out=$("$HSIM" test --help 2>&1) || fail "test --help non-zero: $out"
echo "$out" | grep -q -- '--filter' || fail "help missing --filter:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q -- '--mode'   || fail "help missing --mode:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q -- '--jobs'   || fail "help missing --jobs:"$'\n'"$out"
ok "test --help lists --filter / --mode / --jobs"

# 2. --mode bogus rejected by argparse choices.
set +e
out=$("$HSIM" test --mode bogus --dry-run 2>&1)
rc=$?
set -e
[ "$rc" -ne 0 ] || fail "test --mode bogus should exit non-zero; output: $out"
ok "test --mode bogus exits non-zero (rc=$rc)"

# 3. --dry-run defaults: JOBS=8, MODE=both, FILTER empty.
out=$("$HSIM" test --dry-run 2>&1) || fail "test --dry-run non-zero: $out"
echo "$out" | grep -q '^JOBS=8$'    || fail "default JOBS not 8:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q '^MODE=both$' || fail "default MODE not both:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q '^FILTER=$'   || fail "default FILTER not empty:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q 'bash .*scripts/run_e2e\.sh' || fail "missing exec line:"$'\n'"$out"
ok "test --dry-run defaults JOBS=8 MODE=both FILTER="

# 4. --jobs 4 overrides the cap.
out=$("$HSIM" test --jobs 4 --dry-run 2>&1) || fail "test --jobs 4 non-zero: $out"
echo "$out" | grep -q '^JOBS=4$' || fail "JOBS not 4 with --jobs 4:"$'\n'"$out"
ok "test --jobs 4 overrides default"

# 5. --filter / --mode propagate.
out=$("$HSIM" test --filter '^rt_c_hello$' --mode marker --dry-run 2>&1) \
  || fail "test --filter --mode non-zero: $out"
echo "$out" | grep -q '^FILTER=\^rt_c_hello\$$' || fail "FILTER not propagated:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q '^MODE=marker$'              || fail "MODE not propagated:"$'\n'"$out"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F3 contract: the SAME vplat_hello.elf runs the hybrid handoff:
#
#   andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger pc \
#     --pc-start say_hello --pc-end vplat_roi_end
#
# QEMU1 fast-forwards the newlib boot, drains at say_hello; vsim resumes,
# runs printf -- the bytes go out the MODELED UART, cycle-accurately --
# and drains at vplat_roi_end. Asserts all three: the hello text (from the
# vsim leg), a window_cycles figure, and the PASS line.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. "$ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null
export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:?config.env missing}"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/vplat_hello.elf"
ENG=vsim:ax45mpv_premium
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "driver not built: $BIN"
[ -x "$ROOT/build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64" ] || fail "qemu not built"
[ -x "$ROOT/verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium" ] || fail "vsim not built"
[ -f "$ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so" ] || fail "plugin not built"

make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" vplat_hello.elf >/dev/null || fail "fixture build failed"

OUT=$(timeout 180 "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger pc --engine "$ENG" \
        --pc-start say_hello --pc-end vplat_roi_end "$ELF" </dev/null 2>&1)
RC=$?

printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q 'hello from vplat' \
  || fail "hybrid: missing 'hello from vplat' (the vsim leg must service the UART): $OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -Eq '^\[pc window_cycles\] [0-9]+  \(vsim mcycle=' \
  || fail "hybrid: missing window_cycles line: $OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -Eq '^PASS: --mode hybrid --trigger pc ' \
  || fail "hybrid: missing PASS line: $OUT"
[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "hybrid: exit code $RC != 0 (output: $OUT)"

ok "F3 vplat_hello.elf on hybrid (printf measured on the vsim leg)"

toolUseResult.originalFile:
# ROADMAP: externalize verilator (drop the submodule, mirror the QEMU pattern)

Follows the same move already done for QEMU (commits "drop the QEMU submodule,
integrate a prebuilt external QEMU" + "set QEMU_BIN_DIR"). andesim stops nesting
verilator as a submodule; it consumes a prebuilt vsim from an external location
(e.g. `/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/build`) via `VSIM_BIN_DIR`, exactly like
`QEMU_BIN_DIR` points at the external qemu.

## Why / end state

```
BEFORE:  andesim/verilator  (submodule, andesim builds + records it)
AFTER:   andesim            (no verilator submodule)
         vsim_andesim/      (external sibling repo = hybrid_vsim; built there)
         config.env: VSIM_BIN_DIR=/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/build   <- new, mirrors QEMU_BIN_DIR
```

## Relationship to the abi-split work (already done)

- KEEP: F1 (andesim_abi repo) + F2 (andesim include/ submodule). qemu_plugin and
  the driver still consume the ABI from include/.
- KEEP in hybrid_vsim: F3 (external/andesim_abi submodule + CMake swap). vsim_andesim
  needs it to build standalone. Must reach hybrid_vsim origin (see EX5).
- REVERT: F4's andesim verilator-pointer bump (commit 815259d). With no submodule,
  andesim records no verilator commit. EX3 removes the gitlink entirely.

## Safety gate (before EX3, the destructive step)

`619db38` (the F3 ABI-split commit) is only in local checkouts (andesim/verilator
branch andesim; vsim_andesim branch abi-split-verify), NOT on origin. Before
deleting andesim/verilator, push the F3 work to hybrid_vsim origin's `andesim`
branch so vsim_andesim (and any clone) is reproducible. After that, deleting the
local andesim/verilator loses nothing.

## env-var design (mirror QEMU exactly)

| External thing | env (config.env) | setup.sh exports | driver reads |
|----------------|------------------|------------------|--------------|
| qemu           | `QEMU_BIN_DIR`   | `VSIM_QEMU`      | builtin_qemu path |
| vsim (NEW)     | `VSIM_BIN_DIR`   | `VSIM_BIN_DIR` (+ `ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR`) | engine scan dir |

Driver already has `ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR` (scan any executable). New: an explicit
`VSIM_BIN_DIR` seam that keeps the `sim_` prefix, falling back to the old
`<repo>/verilator/build` when unset (dev back-compat until the submodule is gone).

## Features (one session each; TDD on the driver C++)

### EX1 -- driver: discover engines from VSIM_BIN_DIR
- STATE: DONE (commit ff89fd0). vsim_scan_dir() seam + discover_engines +
  cmd_doctor wired; andesim-engine-registry-test green; `andesim doctor` +
  discovery follow $VSIM_BIN_DIR (verified against /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/build).
- Type: behavioural
- Desc: add a pure `vsim_scan_dir()` seam: `VSIM_BIN_DIR` if set, else
  `repo_root()/verilator/build`. `discover_engines()` and `cmd_doctor` use it.
  Drop cmd_doctor's `verilator/CMakeLists.txt` submodule-presence check.
- Key files: `driver/engine_registry.cpp`, `driver/cmd_doctor.cpp`,
  `driver/engine_registry_test.cpp` (new)
- TDD RED: `vsim_scan_dir()` returns `$VSIM_BIN_DIR` when the env is set; today no
  such function exists / discover_engines hardcodes verilator/build.
- Verify: new doctest green; `andesim-plan-itest` still green.
- Non-destructive (fallback preserved).

### EX2 -- setup.sh + config.env.example: external VSIM_BIN_DIR
- STATE: DONE (commit 4961631). setup.sh locates external vsim from $VSIM_BIN_DIR
  (validates sim_*), exports it, no longer builds vsim; `clean vsim` neutered;
  config.env.example documents VSIM_BIN_DIR. Verified via `source ./setup.sh`.
- Desc: config.env.example gains `VSIM_BIN_DIR=` (mirrors QEMU_BIN_DIR). setup.sh
  reads it from config.env instead of hardcoding `$ROOT/verilator/build`,
  validates a `sim_*` exists (like the qemu-system check), exports `VSIM_BIN_DIR`

Andes hybrid RISC-V simulator: QEMU 9.x (functional, MHz-level) + vsim (SystemC + Verilator, cycle-accurate) share architectural state across a magic-CSR boundary. The system runs a two-phase handoff: **QEMU1** (drain on CSR/PC trigger) -> **vsim** (resume + execute + drain). The cycle figure is the vsim `mcycle` delta; there is no QEMU2 leg (the handback was removed).

Two Git submodules:

Shared ABI lives at `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (not inside either submodule).

  orchestration (`src/hybrid/*.hpp`), `CMakeLists.txt`, and `cmake/HybridConfig.cmake`
  referenced throughout this doc -- live in the separate `hybrid_vsim` repo and are
  built there (its own `build_vsim.sh`), no longer nested under `verilator/` here.

# hybrid_sim

Workspace for the Andes hybrid simulator: QEMU 9.x (functional, MHz) + vsim
(SystemC + Verilator, cycle-accurate) sharing memory and architectural state
across a magic-CSR boundary.

submodules. vsim sources live in the separate `hybrid_vsim` repo, built there.

The repo ships a template `config.env.example` listing per-host paths
that cannot live in the build system (notably the Andes RISC-V
toolchain root, which `setup.sh` does NOT build).

On the first `source ./setup.sh`, the template is copied to
`./config.env` (gitignored) so your edits never touch git history. If
the toolchain lives somewhere other than the default, edit
`config.env`:

```sh
# config.env
HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=/local/nick/SW_Release/build-ast540/build-toolchain/linux/nds64le-elf-newlib-v5d
```

The single variable today is:

| Variable          | What it points at                                                  |
|-------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN`| Toolchain root. `$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/` must contain `riscv64-unknown-elf-{gcc,ld,nm,objdump,...}`. |

How it propagates:

- `setup.sh` sources `config.env`, validates `$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/`
  exists, and `export`s the variable so all child processes see it.
- The fixture `Makefile` (`tests/fixtures/Makefile`) defaults
  `TOOLCHAIN` to `$(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)` and aborts with a clear error if
  the variable is missing.
- The unified `e2e.sh` test harness loads `config.env` itself when run
  without prior `source ./setup.sh`, then derives
  `NM=$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm`.

Override per-invocation without editing the file:

```sh
HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=/opt/my-toolchain make -C tests/fixtures
HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=/opt/my-toolchain ./andesim run \
  tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf --mode hybrid --trigger pc --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium \
  --pc-start vmatmul_kernel --pc-end 0x<post-jal>  # see docs/switching_modes_tutorial.md
```

### 1.4 Build everything

One command builds all three artifacts and exports the env vars the
test harness expects:

```sh
source ./setup.sh
```

`source` (not `bash`) is required so the script can prepend the build
dirs to PATH and export `VSIM_QEMU`, `VSIM_PLUGIN`, `VSIM_BIN`,
`HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN` into the current shell. The steps it
runs:

```
0/3 config     -> auto-copy config.env.example -> config.env (first run);
                  source it; export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN + QEMU_BIN_DIR
1/3 QEMU       -> located (external prebuilt): $QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-riscv64
2/3 vsim       -> verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium    (in container)
3/3 plugin     -> qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so
```

QEMU is not built here: build it yourself and point `QEMU_BIN_DIR` (in
`config.env`) at the directory holding `qemu-system-riscv64`.

```sh
./scripts/build_vsim.sh        # uses podman + Dockerfile (target `env`)
make -C qemu_plugin            # plugins; vendored qemu-plugin.h, no QEMU source needed
```
